source.title: Feature Noise Boosts DNN Generalization Under Label Noise
source.authors: Lu Zeng; Xuan Chen; Xiao-Shuang Shi; Heng-Tao Shen

record.tranche_reason: Tests feature noise as a way to improve generalization under label noise across several datasets and label noise conditions; this is a new intervention and setting relative to the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test memorization of fixed random labels or the claim versions V1–V8. Its results concern feature noise added during training with noisy labels, measured by clean-test accuracy and an approximated PAC-Bayes bound. It cites prior work on fitting random labels, dropout, and other generalization findings; those cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests input feature noise as an intervention for learning with corrupted labels, rather than any V1–V8 claim. It does not measure near-perfect random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization, manipulate width, compare architectures or optimizers, vary batch size, test dropout, measure magnitude-aware sharpness, or remove examples selected by memorization influence. Its PAC-Bayes analysis does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that feature noise can improve generalization under label noise by constraining an information-based PAC-Bayes bound, with stronger benefits under severe label noise and an optimal noise level depending on label corruption. Qualify this as their theoretical interpretation and empirical finding in tested settings; accuracy gains are not universal and the visualized bound is approximate.
record.recipe_differences: The paper adds noise to input features during training and evaluates accuracy under corrupted labels; it does not implement the random-label memorization or interventions in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect varies with label-noise rate, feature-noise type and severity, and feature-noise standard deviation; gains are strongest under severe label noise, while higher noise is not always better.

fits_no_version.finding: Input feature noise improves many clean-test accuracy results under corrupted training labels. MNIST at Δ=0.8 improves from 42.5±5.7% to 95.7±0.4%; ADNI without label corruption falls from 84.9±0.7% to 81.6±0.5%. Effects depend on noise type and level.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitably chosen input feature noise can improve generalization under label corruption, with dataset- and corruption-dependent benefits and occasional losses.

fits_no_version.finding: The joint label-and-feature-noise condition has the tightest approximated PAC-Bayes bound among three MNIST conditions. The authors caution that their Gaussian-prior approximation can be loose.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input feature noise can tighten an approximated PAC-Bayes bound during training with corrupted labels.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: The bound visualization is an approximation and the paper says it can be quite loose because the Gaussian prior is not optimal. Several experiment values are only in figures and are not numerically stated in the text. Feature-noise levels for the table results are not stated in the table. Experiments were repeated three times; standard deviations are reported in the accuracy tables.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for ELR, ES, and other label-noise methods combined with feature noise are omitted; they do not correspond to the catalog versions, and the baseline feature-noise comparisons plus the bound and noise-type findings capture the new intervention. The table’s aggregate improvements versus best comparison methods are omitted because they combine different methods and do not identify the feature-noise intervention’s effect as directly as baseline comparisons.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels and paired held-out performance on natural versus random labels with the same recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and tuning-dependent qualifications.
Batch-size effects at fixed epoch budgets and adapted large-batch recipes.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. Dropout is removed from experimental methods rather than compared.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, correlation with measured generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing examples selected by memorization influence versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are assessed relative to V1–V8, so rows linked to none receive cannot_determine. This does not dispute their reported feature-noise effects. Related-work citations and removal of dropout do not constitute tests of the cited claims.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and comparison of held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test-error behavior as width increases.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and architectural-bias interventions.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer tuning or switching.
Batch-size comparisons and large-batch training recipes.
Dropout interventions and their effects across training-set sizes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining effects.

rows.subject: LeNet-5 (BL)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with symmetric label noise at Δ=0.8, without feature noise.
rows.measure: Approximated PAC-Bayes generalization bound over epochs
rows.note: Text says the bound increases as training proceeds, though it can be very tight early in training; the curve value is figure only.
rows.check: An approximated PAC-Bayes bound does not measure any listed version. Section VII-C uses 30,000-sample conditions and 100 training runs to estimate weight distributions; the generic convergence description omits this protocol.

source_check.locator_found: Section VII-C, Fig. 3, pp. 9–10

rows.subject: LeNet-5 (BL)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with symmetric label noise at Δ=0.8 and Gaussian feature noise with σ²=1.
rows.measure: Approximated PAC-Bayes generalization bound over epochs
rows.baseline: figure only (training with label noise, no feature noise)
rows.note: The authors state this condition yields the tightest bound compared with clean training and label-noise-only training.
rows.check: The tighter approximated PAC-Bayes bound is outside V1–V8; it is not magnitude-aware sharpness. Section VII-C uses 30,000-sample conditions and 100 runs.

rows.subject: LeNet-5 (BL)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST without label noise or feature noise.
rows.measure: Approximated PAC-Bayes generalization bound over epochs
rows.note: The text compares this scenario with label and feature noise jointly but does not state its relative value against clean training alone.
rows.check: The clean-training bound is outside V1–V8. The text does establish that the joint label-and-feature-noise condition has a tighter bound than this condition; the note's reference to comparing clean training with itself is erroneous.

rows.subject: LeNet-5 (BL)

rows.measure: Classification accuracy on the clean test set
rows.baseline: figure only (label noise, no feature noise)
rows.locator: Section VII-D, Fig. 2; Section VII-F, Fig. 5
rows.note: Paper states Gaussian noise improves generalization at high severity under Δ=0.8, and that accuracy peaks then decreases as σ increases; exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Input feature noise is outside V1–V8. The cited accuracy figures sweep noise severity or standard deviation; they do not establish a distinct accuracy result at the fixed σ²=1 condition used in Fig. 3.

rows.subject: LeNet-5 (BL)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with symmetric label noise and Gaussian feature noise; six feature-noise standard deviations and six label-noise rates were evaluated.
rows.measure: Testing accuracy across feature-noise and label-noise levels
rows.note: The text says the best σ rises with label-noise rate, but a higher σ is not always better because accuracy peaks and then decreases.
rows.check: This aggregates a feature-noise parameter sweep outside V1–V8. Its nonmonotonic accuracy response is not evidence about dropout.

relation.reason: The introduction and related work discuss random-label fitting, dropout and generalization explanations without testing a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: Feature-noise interventions and PAC-Bayes bound analyses measure a related construct outside V1–V8; the study neither tests nor uses those findings as a tool.

source_check.notes: All sampled values match the source, including the unusually high clean-label FashionMNIST accuracies. The bound is a Gaussian approximation; neither it nor the feature-noise accuracy comparisons establishes any V1–V8 effect.
